title: An abstract research field: OSO vs. traditional research
html:
An abstract research field: OSO vs. traditional research

A generic field of 80 ideas in 8 levels and 3 areas, with 7 bounties; the simulator's default world.

For the same money, the OSO community got further, or got there more cheaply, than the traditional one.

  • How far: with a budget of 1200 money, OSO reached level 7.9 of 8 on average; traditional research reached 5.7.
  • Targets solved: OSO solved 6.9 of 7; traditional solved 4.2.
  • Cost to reach level 7: OSO 485 money; traditional 957 money (in the 35% of runs that got there).
  • Return on the money (ROI): OSO gained 1.44 in bounty value per unit spent (1130 for 849); traditional 0.22 (268 for 1194). Value gained is the bounties of the targets solved.
  • Does flow-back make agents share? When agents choose, sharing rises clearly (by 0.2 or more) once α is 0.3 or lower. At OSO's default α = 0.8, agents shared 22% of their intermediate ideas.
  • Robustness: OSO's lead in level is smallest when shared knowledge is costly to take up (+2.0 levels).
  • Sensitivity: Across the tested values of the parameters a market or community sets, OSO's lead (agents choosing what to share) runs from +0.3 to +1.9 levels. The smallest lead, at ρ, money follows earnings = 100%, is still clearly positive. The lead is most sensitive to α, absorption rate.

The verdict compares the hardest level reached, the targets solved and (when both communities reach level 7 in at least 90% of runs) the cost to get there, each against two standard errors. 100 simulated runs per setting · simulator commit 4bd670b+ · 2026-10-23. This is a simulation with guessed parameters, not evidence about real research; see What this shows.

1. The problem space

A research field with no particular subject. Ideas build on ideas in eight levels of rising difficulty, across three loosely connected areas. Seven targets carry bounties that double with each level, and about a third of all ideas are dead ends that lead to no target. Twelve agents of six kinds work in it: patient foundation builders, target racers, cheap explorers, specialists, a free rider and a gamer who farms trivial ideas.

In this space means
an idea a finding that later findings can build on
a target a bounty-carrying finding announced in advance
an attempt one attempt at proving a finding, which succeeds or fails
an area a subfield

The tree has 80 ideas in 8 levels and 3 areas (area 1, area 2, area 3). 29 are dead ends: no target depends on them. 7 are targets:

2. Progress for the money

Each line is the mean, over 100 runs, of the hardest level the community had published after spending that much money. A line that ends early means every target was solved and the funder stopped paying.

3. The six settings

The rules are the only difference between rows (specification, section 3). Traditional: nothing flows back to what an idea built on, and work is published only when finished. OSO: value flows back (α = 0.8, c = 0.15), and ideas are published at once or when the agent chooses.

Sharing rises clearly once α is 0.3 or lower: this is the threshold α* in this space. The threshold depends on the scoop risk ψ = 0.5, which is a guess.

5. When sharing is costly or sometimes wrong

Taking up a published idea costs 0.5; proofs are wrong 10% of the time, ideas built on a wrong idea are wrong too, and targets reveal and retract them.

6. Sensitivity to the parameters

In OSO, α and c are set by each community (OIP-14), validators decide how strict the screen is, funders decide how far money follows earnings, and the mint may become a community parameter (OIP-8). Their values will be set by competing communities, not by us, so the result must hold across them. The parameters below the line are our guesses about how agents think.

Each parameter is varied alone, from this space's settings, with agents choosing what to share (the realistic case: incentives matter only if sharing is a choice). The lead is OSO's hardest level reached minus traditional's under the same parameter value; α and c do not exist under traditional rules, so there it is compared with traditional's default.

Across the tested values of the parameters a market or community sets, OSO's lead (agents choosing what to share) runs from +0.3 to +1.9 levels. The smallest lead, at ρ, money follows earnings = 100%, is still clearly positive. The lead is most sensitive to α, absorption rate.

What this shows and what it does not

  • It is a simulation of the OSO demo specification: ideas are abstract, success is chance, and agents follow a formula. It shows how the incentive rules play out if this space works as described, not that it does.
  • The parameters are guesses, especially the success chances, the scoop risk ψ, and the costs and error rates in section 5. Section 6 varies each one alone; it does not vary them together, except α and c.
  • By default, sharing is free and always correct, which favours OSO; section 5 shows how much of the lead survives without that.

Reproduce

npm run sim -- report abstract-field --seeds 100

The space is spaces/abstract-field.yaml (written by hand; the default scenario). Every number above is in data.json. Generated by the OSO simulator at commit 4bd670b+ (with uncommitted changes).
